headword: {抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}

definitions.explanation: A type of medication used to treat bacterial infections by killing or inhibiting the growth of bacteria.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}に{抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}を{処方|しょほう}された。
{抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}は{最後|さいご}まで{飲|の}みきってください。
examples.english: Please take the full course of antibiotics.

examples.japanese: {抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}の{使|つか}いすぎは{耐性菌|たいせいきん}を{生|う}む{原因|げんいん}になる。
examples.english: Overuse of antibiotics is a cause of antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

notes:
USAGE:
{抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ} is the formal/technical term for antibiotics. In everyday conversation, people often simply say {抗生剤|こうせいざい} or informally refer to them as their specific medication name.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}を{飲|の}む (to take antibiotics)
- {抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}を{処方|しょほう}する (to prescribe antibiotics)
- {抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}{耐性|たいせい} (antibiotic resistance)

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:
Antibiotics treat bacterial infections, not viral ones. Japanese doctors sometimes explain this as {抗生物質|こうせいぶっしつ}は{風邪|かぜ}には{効|き}かない (antibiotics don't work for colds).
